 Order
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the State.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioners for setting aside/quashing the order dated 05.10.2023 passed by the Collector and District Magistrate, Bolangir, Opposite Party No.3 under Annexure-7 wherein it has been held that the calculation of compensation has been made correctly as per Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 basing on the approval of the Special Secretary to Government in Works Department, Odisha, Bhubaneswar and the revised compensation has already been paid to the petitioners as per their claim.
Learned counsel for the petitioners urged that determination of compensation has been made in respect of the acquired land by the authority taking into account that the land is shown in the R.O.R.
as Bahal Mamuli instead of Gharabari and the adjacent four plots have already been converted to Gharabari.

sentences.text: On perusal of the impugned order, it appears that the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners made a submission before the Collector that the petitioners contacted the Tahasildar, Bolangir several times for conversion of their land to kisam Gharabari, but the Tahasildar refused for conversion of the entire land at a time rather advised to apply for conversion of 5000 sq. feet of land at a time and so on and the petitioners could not show any document/application in support of such allegation.

Even in the writ petition in paragraph-4, it is mentioned that the Tahasildar, Bolangir did not allow to convert plot no.1985 to Gharabari knowing fully well that the land in question will be taken over by the opposite parties.

However, during course of argument, learned counsel made a submission that the application for conversion under section 8-A of the Orissa Land Reforms Act, 1960 is pending with the Tahasildar,
Bolangir, which is contrary to the submission made by the petitioners' counsel before Opposite Party No.3 also the averments made in paragraph-4 of the writ petition.
There is no dispute that against the order passed by the Tahasildar, Bolangir, appeal lies to the Sub-Collector under section 58 of the Orissa Land Reforms Act, 1960.

Learned counsel for the State has also pointed out section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which deals with reference to the authority in case, a person does not accept the award, can make a written application to the Collector requiring him the matter to be referred by the Collector for determination of the authority.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State further submitted that in this case, the petitioners have already accepted the compensation fixed by the authority.

Be that as it may, learned counsel for the petitioners seeks for an adjournment till next week to obtain instruction whether the application under section 8-A of Orissa Land Reforms Act is subjudiced before the Tahasildar, Bolangir or it has been disposed of and if so, whether the petitioners have challenged the said order before the competent authority or not.
List this matter in the week commencing from 20th August 2024.
( S.K. Sahoo)
Judge  (Chittaranjan Dash)
